title: sipmsgops Module
content_markdown: The module implements SIP based operations over the messages processed by OpenSIPS. SIP is a text based protocol and the module provides a large set of very useful functions to manipulate the message at SIP level, e.g., inserting new headers or deleting them, check for method type, etc.
overview: The module implements SIP based operations over the messages processed by OpenSIPS. SIP is a text based protocol and the module provides a large set of very useful functions to manipulate the message at SIP level, e.g., inserting new headers or deleting them, check for method type, etc.

exported_functions.name: append_to_reply

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: SIP header field, value and CRLF marker.

exported_functions.description: Append 'txt' as header to all replies that will be generated by OpenSIPS for this request.

exported_functions.name: append_hf

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: Header field to be appended.

parameters.name: hdr_anchor
parameters.description: Header name after which the 'txt' is appended.

exported_functions.description: Appends 'txt' as header after the last header field. If 'hdr_anchor' is given, 'txt' will be appended after the first occurrence of 'hdr_anchor' instead.

exported_functions.name: insert_hf

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: Header field to be inserted.

exported_functions.description: Inserts 'txt' as header before the first header field.

exported_functions.name: insert_hf

parameters.name: txt
parameters.description: Header field to be inserted.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Header name before which the 'txt' is inserted.

exported_functions.description: Inserts 'txt' as header before first 'hdr' header field.

exported_functions.name: append_urihf

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: string (usually at least header field name).

parameters.name: suffix
parameters.description: string (usually at least line terminator).

exported_functions.description: Append header field name with original Request-URI in middle.

exported_functions.name: is_present_hf

parameters.name: hf_name
parameters.description: Header field name (long or compact form).

return_values.condition: if a header field is present in message

exported_functions.description:
Return true if a header field is present in message.

The function is also able to distinguish the compact names. For exmaple “From” will match with “f”

examples.description: Check if From header is present

exported_functions.name: append_time

return_values.condition: if a header was successfully appended

exported_functions.description:
Adds a time header to the reply of the request. You must use it before functions that are likely to send a reply, e.g., save() from 'registrar' module. Header format is: “Date: %a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT”, with the legend:

*   _%a_ abbreviated week of day name (locale)
*   _%d_ day of month as decimal number
*   _%b_ abbreviated month name (locale)
*   _%Y_ year with century
*   _%H_ hour
*   _%M_ minutes
*   _%S_ seconds

exported_functions.name: is_method

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: SIP method name

return_values.condition: if the method of the message matches the name

exported_functions.description:
Check if the method of the message matches the name. If name is a known method (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack), the function performs method ID testing (integer comparison) instead of ignore case string comparison.

The 'name' can be a list of methods in the form of 'method1|method2|...'. In this case, the function returns true if the SIP message's method is one from the list. IMPORTANT NOTE: in the list must be only methods defined in OpenSIPS with ID (invite, cancel, ack, bye, options, info, update, register, message, subscribe, notify, refer, prack, publish; for more see: [https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters](https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters)).

If used for replies, the function tests the value of method field from CSeq header.

exported_functions.name: remove_hf

parameters.name: hname
parameters.description: header name to be removed.

return_values.condition: if at least one header is found and removed

exported_functions.description: Remove from message all headers with name “hname”

exported_functions.name: remove_hf_re

parameters.name: hname_expr
parameters.description: regular expression.

return_values.condition: if at least one header is found and removed

exported_functions.description: Remove from message all headers matching the “hname_expr” POSIX regular expression.

exported_functions.name: remove_hf_glob

parameters.name: hname_pattern
parameters.description: glob pattern

return_values.condition: if at least one header is found and removed

exported_functions.description: Remove from message all headers matching the “hname_pattern” glob pattern.

examples.code:
...
# removes X-Billing-Account, X-Billing-Price, X-Billing-rateplan, etc
remove_hf_glob("X-Billing*");
...

exported_functions.description: Check if To header field uri contains tag parameter.

exported_functions.name: ruri_has_param

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: parameter name to look for

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: parameter value to match

exported_functions.description: Find if Request URI has a given parameter. If no value is given, the function will look for the paramter with no value, oherwise it will search for the parameter with the matching value.

exported_functions.name: ruri_add_param

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: parameter to be appended in “name=value” format

exported_functions.description: Add to RURI an URI parameter formated as "name=value".

exported_functions.name: ruri_del_param

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: the parameter to be removed

exported_functions.description: Delete a parameter, its value and any leading ";" from the Request-URI of the current SIP message.

exported_functions.name: ruri_tel2sip

return_values.condition: conversion succeeded or if no conversion was needed (like RURI was not tel URI

exported_functions.description: Converts RURI, if it is tel URI, to SIP URI. Returns true, only if conversion succeeded or if no conversion was needed (like RURI was not tel URI.

exported_functions.name: is_uri_user_e164

parameters.name: uri
parameters.description: a SIP URI

exported_functions.description: Checks if the username part of the given URI is an E164 number.

exported_functions.name: has_body_part

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: MIME type

return_values.condition: SIP message has any body part with the given MIME. If there is no MIME given, it will return true if at least one body part is found (with any MIME).

exported_functions.description: The function returns true if the SIP message has any body part with the given MIME. If there is no MIME given, it will return true if at least one body part is found (with any MIME).

exported_functions.name: is_audio_on_hold

return_values.condition: RFC2543 hold type: null connection IP detected
RFC3264 hold type: inactive or sendonly attributes detected

exported_functions.description: The function returns true if the SIP message has an SDP body attached and at least one audio stream in on hold. The return code of the function indicates the detected hold type:

exported_functions.name: is_privacy

parameters.name: privacy_type
parameters.description: privacy type

return_values.condition: SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values.

exported_functions.description: The function returns true if the SIP message has a Privacy header field that includes the given privacy_type among its privacy values. See https://www.iana.org/assignments/sip-parameters/sip-parameters.xhtml#sip-parameters-8 for possible privacy type values.

exported_functions.name: remove_body_part

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: MIME type to be checked against the body parts; If not given, all parts are to remvoed;

parameters.name: revert
parameters.description: useful only if a MIME was specified. If "revert" string is given here, the function will delete all body parts but the ones with the given MIME.

exported_functions.description:
Removes from the message body all the body parts with the given mime. The necessary corrections over the Content-Type and Content-Length headers are automatically done.

If a MIME type is given, it will delete only the body parts with that mime. If no MIME given, all the parts (entire body) will be removed.

exported_functions.name: add_body_part

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: the content of the body part to be added

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: the mime string for the body part to be added

parameters.name: headers
parameters.description: optional list of SIP headers (fully defined, including the header separator) to be pushed into this part next to the _Content-Type_ header.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to add a new body part to the message body. If another part already exist, body of the message will be converted to a multi-part body automatically.

exported_functions.name: get_updated_body_part

parameters.name: mime
parameters.description: the mime string for the body to be regenerated and returned. If missing, the whole body (with all its parts) will be regenerated.

parameters.name: variable
parameters.description: a variable to be used to return the regenerated body part (as text).

exported_functions.description:
This function returns into a variable the regenerated body part, meaning the body part updated with all the changes done so far by OpenSIPS. This is helpful if you want to do a sequance of operations over the body parts and some operations require to have all the previous changes applied (like first doing some codec related changes and later to rtpengine insertion).

NOTE: the actual SIP message will not be affected by this operation!

exported_functions.name: sipmsg_validate

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: composed with the following values: 's' (checks SDP), 'h' (checks headers), 'm' (skip Max-Forwards), 'r' (checks R-URI), 'f' (checks From), 't' (checks To), 'c' (checks Contact).

parameters.name: result_pvar
parameters.description: sets resulting pvar with text error reason in case of negative result ( easy for logging or propagating the rejection reason back to the bogus UA )

return_values.condition: the message is RFC3261 compliant and has been successfully validated.
No Content-Length header for transports that require it ( eg. TCP )
Invalid Content-Length, other from the size of the actual body
Contact header contains * for non-Register request

exported_functions.description: The function returns _true_ if the SIP message is properly built according to SIP RFC3261. It verifies if the mandatory headers for each request/reply and can also check the format of the headers body.

exported_functions.name: codec_exists

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to verify if a codec exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

exported_functions.name: codec_delete

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all will be deleted. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to delete a codec from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted from the mapping ("a=...") and from the list of indexes ("m=...").

exported_functions.name: codec_move_up

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the front while preserving their original ordering. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to move a codec up in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the top of the index list.

exported_functions.name: codec_move_down

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

parameters.name: clock
parameters.description: if not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the back while preserving their original ordering. Parameter is CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to move a codec down in the list of indexes ("m=..."). It will search for the codec inside all streams from all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be moved to the back of the index list. The second parameter is optional, if it is not supplied any clockrate will match and all codecs will be moved to the back while preserving their original ordering. Parameters are CASE INSENSITIVE.

exported_functions.name: codec_exists_re

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: POSIX regular expression

exported_functions.description: This function has the same effect as codec_exists ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

exported_functions.name: codec_delete_re

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: POSIX regular expression

exported_functions.description: This function has the same effect as codec_delete ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

exported_functions.name: codec_delete_except_re

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: POSIX regular expression

exported_functions.description: This function deletes all the codecs except those specified by the regular expression.

examples.code:
...
codec_delete_except_re("PCMA|PCMU");#will delete all codecs except PCMA and PCMU
...

exported_functions.name: codec_move_up_re

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: POSIX regular expression

exported_functions.description: This function has the same effect as codec_move_up ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

exported_functions.name: codec_move_down_re

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: POSIX regular expression

exported_functions.description: This function has the same effect as codec_move_down ( without the clock parameter ) the only difference is that it takes a POSIX regular expression as a parameter.

exported_functions.name: change_reply_status

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Status code.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Reason phrase.

exported_functions.description: Intercept a SIP reply (in any onreply_route) and change its status code and reason phrase prior to propogating it.

exported_functions.name: stream_exists

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: a POSIX regular expression to match the stream media name.

parameters.name: regexp2
parameters.description: an optional POSIX regular expression to match the stream transport name.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to verify if a stream exists inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will return TRUE otherwise it will return FALSE.

exported_functions.name: stream_delete

parameters.name: regexp
parameters.description: a POSIX regular expression to match the stream media name.

parameters.name: regexp2
parameters.description: an optional POSIX regular expression to match the stream transport name.

exported_functions.description: This function can be used to delete a whole stream from inside an sdp payload. It will search for the stream inside all sdp sessions. If it is found anywhere it will be deleted along with all attributes

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_has_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header to be checked. Note that all instances of that header will be checked (if the header has multiple instances in the SIP message). Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: option
parameters.description: the option/tolen to be searched for.

return_values.condition: if the options was found listed in one of the header instances
If no header was found, if the option was not found or if there was a parsing or runtime error

exported_functions.description: Checks and returns true if the given option/token is listed in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_add_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header where the option has to be added. If multiple instances of that header are present in the SIP message, the add will be performed on the first instance. Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: option
parameters.description: the option/token to be added to the CSV list. Note there is not verification for duplicated (if the newly added option is not already present in the header).

return_values.condition: if the options was successfully added to the listed of the given header
If no header was found or if there was a parsing or runtime error

exported_functions.description:
Add a new option/token at the end of the list in the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Disposition headers) body format

Multiple add / remove operations can be performed over the same header.

exported_functions.name: list_hdr_remove_option

parameters.name: hdr_name
parameters.description: the name of the header where the option has to be removed from. If the option is duplicated in the same header, only the last one will be removed. If multiple instances of that header are present in the SIP message, the remove will be performed on all instance instance. Any kind of header name is supported - RFC3261 standard, RFC extensions or custom names.

parameters.name: option
parameters.description: the option/token to be removed from the CSV list. Note that if this the only option in the header, the whole header will be removed.

return_values.condition: if the options was successfully removed from at least one heaer instance
If no header was found or if the token was not found or if there was a parsing or runtime error

exported_functions.description:
Removes an option/token from the list inside the body of the given header. The header must have its body formated as a CSV list of tokens/option (like the Supported, Require, Content-Dispsition headers) body format

Multiple add / remove operations can be performed over the same header.

exported_functions.name: get_glob_headers_values

parameters.name: hdr_name_glob
parameters.description: the glob pattern for matching the header names

parameters.name: hdr_names_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will get populated with all the header names that match the glob pattern

parameters.name: hdr_vals_avp
parameters.description: the AVP which will get populated with all the header values corresponding to the header names that match the glob pattern

return_values.condition: if at least 1 header was found that matches the glob pattern

exported_functions.description: Populates the hdr_names_avp and hdr_vals_avp AVPs with all the header names and values that match the hdr_name_glob pattern.
